note:
Preview P6 budgets (issue #170, docs/design/reference-equantic-ui.md section 7.4; ADR-045 consequences). Checked by scripts/check_preview_budget.py. TWO-SIDED RATCHET: an entry fails when it is worse than its budget by more than tolerance.worse, AND when it is better by more than tolerance.better (the budget went stale and must be tightened with --update, which never loosens any entry). The two sides carry different percentages on purpose: a single symmetric band wide enough for a noisy timing row (300%) would make the lower bound negative and silently disable the staleness side, so 'better' stays under 100% for every entry. Only download_gzip_bytes is ENFORCED: it is exactly reproducible for a fixed input and zlib build, so its 5%/1% band is measurement slack, not noise cover, and it is the number the slice's acceptance is about. The two latency entries WARN, for two separate reasons. (1) They are the ENGINE'S SHARE ONLY: cold time-to-first-frame also needs the browser's HTML/CSS parse and a WebGPU frame (P3, not landed), and edit-to-view needs that frame too. They are named for what was measured instead of borrowing the slice's name for a number that is not the whole path; the browser lane adds cold_first_frame_ms/edit_to_view_ms beside them. (2) Wall-clock time on a shared CI runner is not reproducible (docs/guides/testing.md section 7). Their mitigations are tolerance.worse = 300% (a multiple, so only an order-of-magnitude change fires) and min-over-N-fresh-processes, which discards contention instead of averaging it in. Their tolerance.better is a plain 20%: the min statistic is already close to the true cost, so a 20% improvement is real news and worth recording. ISSUE #392 (the three-page merge) RE-PINNED download_gzip_bytes from 417327 to the measured value, a deliberate raise reviewed in that PR rather than a regression: the merged page ships all three views plus the two redirect stubs in one artifact, where the old artifact was one page and one module. Of the growth, ~16911 bytes is the page (the three views' modules and their render/pane helpers, the shell that replaces three copies of the header and toolbar wiring, redirect.js and the two stubs, the canvas pane's CSS folded into app.css, minus the deleted app.js/scene.js/canvas.js/canvas.css), and ~2556 bytes is the diagnostics module itself, which no source in this change touched: that module is byte-identical when rebuilt (SHA-256 7A6FF0AD...095E7F both times) and its gzip delta comes from the zlib build on the measuring host, not from the merge. The raise is what the P6 acceptance calls a deliberately updated ratchet: --update by itself refuses it (a raise is a reviewed edit, never a re-pin), so the pin was edited here with this reason and then recorded from the measurement.
 ISSUE #422 (the React 19 + Vite conversion, ADR-054) RE-PINNED download_gzip_bytes from 470312 to 470568, as a reviewed edit rather than a re-pin: --update refuses a raise, so the pin was edited here with this reason and then recorded from the measurement (python -B scripts/check_preview_budget.py --check --size-only --module-dir build/wasm-webgpu/src/compiler/codegen). The measurement itself moved with the stack (ADR-054 decision 6): the old PAGE_FILES list named source files, and a Vite build's assets carry content hashes (assets/index-<hash>.js) that no list can name, so preview_budget_measure.py now walks the built designer/web/dist/ as a whole. The number is still the visitor's first-paint download and still two-sided; what changed is that an asset which ships is weighed by construction instead of by a list being kept up to date.

THE ATTRIBUTION, measured rather than estimated. The page went from 57388 gzip bytes (21 hand-written files) to 91162 (7 files: a hashed JS chunk, a hashed CSS chunk, index.html, the two stubs, redirect.js and samples.json), a delta of +33774, and it decomposes:

* **+69007 is React 19.3.1 + react-dom 19.3.1.** Measured as a control build, from the same lockfile and the same Vite, of `createRoot(...).render(<p/>)` with nothing else in the graph. That is the framework floor the conversion pays for, not this page's code.
* **-30211 is the vanilla JavaScript it replaces.** The page's own JS is the 82797-byte-gzip chunk minus that floor: 13790 bytes, against 44001 gzip bytes of hand-written modules before (studio-page.js, shell.js, wasm-call.js, the three views and their five render/pane/device helpers, studio.js, gallery.js, share.js, preview-state.js, scene-input.js). React's component model is cheaper than the document.createElement tree it replaces on this page.
* **-2631 + (-2391) = -5022 is CSS and HTML, both minified by the build.** app.css 5065 -> 2434 and index.html 3602 -> 1211: the stylesheet is now processed and the document is a mount point instead of 210 lines of hand-written markup. The public files (redirect.js, the two stubs, samples.json) are copied verbatim and did not move: 4720 bytes gzip.

69007 -30211 -5022 = +33774, against the measured page delta of +33774. The diagnostics module is unchanged (379406 gzip bytes, the same two files), which is why the download moved by exactly the page delta. The result is inside the 6 MB product budget (designer-studio-v1.md section 2.3) with 5.5 MB to spare, and the raise is what the P6 acceptance calls a deliberately updated ratchet: a reviewed edit of the budget file with the reason in the diff, never --update loosening a pin.

source.module: tessera_diagnostics_wasm, the P1 page module (src/compiler/codegen/CMakeLists.txt); the same bytes the Pages lane assembles into build/pages. Its two files (the loader and the wasm) are measured from the module directory, not from dist/: they are linked engine artifacts copied next to the page, never bundled
source.page: the built page, designer/web/dist/ (issue #422, ADR-054 decision 6). The measurement walks that directory rather than naming files: Vite emits content-hashed assets (assets/index-<hash>.js, assets/index-<hash>.css) that a fixed list cannot name, and walking the directory keeps the rule the old PAGE_FILES list existed for -- an asset that ships is an asset that is weighed -- true by construction. The tree is index.html (the mount point), the hashed JS and CSS chunks (React 19 chrome plus the three view sessions), the two pre-merge redirect stubs, redirect.js and samples.json, which Vite copies from designer/web/public/. The three Wasm loaders are not in the bundle: they are lazy import()s the Pages lane copies next to the page, and only tessera_diagnostics is weighed because it is the one on the first-paint path
source.runtime: the module runs in the Emscripten Node host ($EMSDK_NODE in CI); a browser host cannot be measured in this lane

download_gzip_bytes.measures: gzip-9 bytes of the whole designer/web/ page directory plus tessera_diagnostics.js + tessera_diagnostics.wasm: the transfer a browser pays for the page and its module

cold_engine_ready_ms.measures: minimum over 5 fresh processes of (module instantiation + first compile); the engine's share of cold time-to-first-frame, NOT the frame

edit_compile_ms.measures: minimum over 5 fresh processes of the per-edit minimum compile of 30 edits after 5 warm-up compiles; the engine's share of edit-to-view, NOT the frame
